role: voice-audit: independent check of the voice comparison before its numbers are shown to the owner
summary: Rules, files, environments and disk are mostly clean: no pickle without weights_only reached at run time, no trust_remote_code, no telemetry code (every grep hit was the word 'amplitude'), .venv-audio is identical to its freeze, nothing forbidden is in the Hugging Face cache, all scored lines exist at 24 kHz and are not silent. Open problems: (1) the two CUDA timings of record are optimistic because the card is shared with the owner's desktop programs (50 % busy when idle, 95-100 % during my first re-time): Kokoro 0.011 became 0.173 under 95-100 % outside load and 0.019 at 50 %; Qwen3 1.825 became 2.96 and 2.42; (2) the Qwen3 adapter never sets HF_HUB_OFFLINE and pins no revision, so every run asks huggingface.co; (3) the Qwen3 CPU run has 3 of 15 lines; (4) Kitten presets (origin not stated) are used as they are; Kokoro and kitten-blend blend presets of unstated origin; (5) the claim 'Chatterbox with 8 threads gave no speedup' is not supported by my re-time (8 threads 0.53, 4 threads 0.71, both under load); (6) score.py counts 3 ordinary errors for qwen3 cuda procedural_convoy where a hand count gives 2, because of an alignment tie. Nobody has heard anything; nothing here judges sound.

runs.rtfAudit: 2.957 (card 95-100 % busy from outside the lock), 2.424 (second run, card about 50 % busy); not within a quarter either time; audio length identical to the builder's, so output is deterministic
runs.reason: Adapter follows the contract (text_for, untouched wav, synchronize before and after, one warm-up, peak memory). Flawed because the RTF of record is optimistic by 30-60 % on a shared card, and the adapter does not set HF_HUB_OFFLINE nor pin the two revisions, so each load contacts huggingface.co. The finding 'slower than real time' holds in every measurement. Cast: four VoiceDesign clips, take 1 for all voices with the same seed 20261115 (the report's 'seeds 20261115 to 20261117' are the takes of one voice, not four seeds).

runs.rtfAudit: 3.729 (4 lines; CPU 77-88 % busy from other agents when queued); the 3 shared lines each 1.21-1.22 times the builder, inside a quarter
runs.reason: Only 3 of 15 lines were run although no line came near five minutes (slowest 30 s, so all 15 would take about 7 minutes). No same-voice figure possible. Environment variable and thread limit are set in code before torch is imported (device_count 0 with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty on this machine); actual thread use was not measured.

Agrees (1.05). Speaks only in the four Qwen3 clips (cast json reference_from qwen3, clip paths point to assets/audio/voice/qwen3/cast, conds.pt not in the snapshot, adapter asserts model.conds is None). CPU-only torch 2.6.0+cpu, hub offline, sockets blocked, no connection attempt. Perth watermark is inside generate() and untouched; its pickle loads by torch's default weights_only=True (torch 2.6.0 verified). vc.py (torch.load without weights_only) is never reached. Timed span is generate() only; conditional preparation is outside, as disclosed.

Run is valid and thread count 8 is recorded and set. The interpretation is not: my re-time gave 8 threads 0.53 against 4 threads 0.71 in two locked runs a few minutes apart, both with 46-48 % outside CPU load, so 'no speedup' (RESULTS.md, CANDIDATES.md) is not established. Four lines only.

runs.rtfAudit: 0.173 (card 95-99 % busy from outside), then 0.019 and 0.019 (card about 50 % busy); ratios 13.4, 1.46, 1.46
runs.reason: Adapter is correct (synchronize inside the loop, G2P and the copy to CPU are inside the timed span, one chunk per line). The figure 0.011 is the best case and is not reproduced within a quarter on this machine; it is about 50 times faster than real time at 50 % outside load and slower than the CPU run at 95-100 % outside load. Voices are blends of built-in packs whose origin is not stated; pickle files are loaded only with weights_only=True (package code and the adapter's guard checked); hub offline.

Agrees (0.98). CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 and an assert that the card is not visible; threads set in env and torch. The builder's remark that an empty string deletes the variable on Windows is not true for this Python (it is kept and torch sees 0 devices), harmless. Voice origin: blends of presets of unstated origin, graded C+ for the male voices.

Timing agrees (1.02). Flawed against the rule 'never a built-in voice whose origin is not stated': the four voices are single presets (Martha, Vincent, Eleanor, Otis) used as they are and the makers do not say where they come from. Output differs between identical calls, so no seed. Joins chunks with its own 0.15 s of silence in the adapter (all test lines are one chunk, so none is added). torch.load with weights_only=False exists only in the 1.7B path (kittentts2/*), which is not imported for Tiny (checked by listing sys.modules).
Agrees (1.00). Blend of two presets of unstated origin; the README allows blending but origin of the parts is still not shown. 4 lines, pilot_m never spoken.

Agrees (1.04). The four voices are character embeddings that the voices card says were made with Gradium Voice Design (I re-read the README at the source: Fairy Godmother, Vyrmathrax, Snow Queen, Grub and Old Mortlake carry the ids used); no catalogue voice was downloaded (cache holds the 12 characters and voices.jsonl). Local model path and hub offline; the native module contains an HF/HTTP client, so that nothing is fetched rests on the adapter passing a local folder (not proven by a network trace). The 'temperature 0.3' written into the voice record is not passed to synth, so it is only a note. CPU only; no graphics-card run exists.
Agrees (0.89). Same checks as phonon; q8 file loaded locally.

runs.rtfAudit: 0.072 (ratio 1.26, a hair outside a quarter; the builder's own f32 runs differ by 20 %)
runs.reason: Valid but thin (4 lines) and not to be ranked. station_dock has 7 samples at or above full scale and peak above 1.0 in the float file; written untouched as the contract says, but it will clip when converted to 16 bit.

adapters.text_for: All five pass common.text_for(line) to the model (warm-up uses common.WARM_UP).
adapters.untouched_output: Qwen3, Chatterbox, Kokoro and Phonon write the returned samples; Kitten concatenates chunks with its own 0.15 s zero gap (single chunk per test line); Kokoro concatenates pieces without a gap. No gain, trim, resample or filter anywhere. Audio files are float32 mono at 24000 Hz everywhere.
adapters.timed_span: Only the synthesis call, torch.cuda.synchronize before and after on the card (Qwen3, Kokoro). Spans differ in content: Kokoro and Kitten include grapheme-to-phoneme and (Kokoro) the copy to CPU; Chatterbox includes the Perth watermark; Qwen3, Chatterbox exclude the per-voice conditioning (done once, disclosed); Phonon includes its text front end.
adapters.cpu_isolation: Chatterbox (torch 2.6.0+cpu) and Phonon (no torch) cannot reach the card; Kitten and Qwen3 set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to an empty string, which on this machine hides the card (device_count 0, tested); Kokoro uses -1 and asserts. Thread limits are set in env and torch/onnx/ptts options in all five; real thread use was not measured.
adapters.voices_of_unstated_origin: Kitten presets as they are (yes), Kokoro presets as blends (yes), kitten-blend (yes). Not used: Chatterbox built-in voice, Phonon catalogue voices, Qwen3 CustomVoice presets.
adapters.pickle_trust_telemetry: No trust_remote_code in any adapter or package path used. torch.load: Kokoro model and packs weights_only=True; Chatterbox uses weights_only=True, Perth relies on torch 2.6.0's default; Qwen3 and Phonon load safetensors; Kitten loads none. Grep for posthog, sentry, telemetry, analytics, mixpanel, amplitude, segment found only the word 'amplitude' in vocoder code. Qwen3's adapter leaves the hub online and unpinned (see mustFix). Kokoro's misaki can call spacy.cli.download only if the model is missing; the wheel was installed beforehand.

checks.venv_audio: pip freeze of .venv-audio sorted equals assets/audio/voice/venv-audio-freeze-before.txt: no difference (76 packages).
checks.files: All expected lines exist for every run (15 each; qwen3 cpu 3; chatterbox-8t, kitten-blend, phonon-blend 4 listen lines). No silent file, no file under 1 s or over 30 s, sample rate 24000 and float32 for all, durations equal timing.json. Words per second outside 1.5-4.5: kokoro computer_cargo_raw 1.44 (a counting artefact: the raw line has 10 written tokens that are spoken as more words), phonon radio_readback 1.46, radio_mayday 1.32, computer_cargo_raw 1.49, phonon-q8 1.46, 1.37, 1.40, phonon-blend computer_fold 1.32. Clipping only phonon-blend station_dock (7 samples, peak above 1). Qwen3 cast clips exist (10.88, 12.88, 13.20, 11.84 s, 24 kHz, peaks 0.61-0.77, VoiceDesign 1.7B, take 1, seed 20261115) and both Chatterbox cast records point to exactly those four files.
checks.retime: Eleven locked re-runs of the four listen lines were made earlier in this audit by a driver that copied each device directory to _audit/before, ran the adapter under the lock, saved timing.json to _audit/retime and restored; I verified by md5 manifests and diff -r that every scored directory is byte-identical to its copy (the driver's 'RESTORE MISMATCH' for kokoro cpu was a false alarm in its own check). Today I added kokoro cuda twice (r2, r3) and qwen3 cuda once (r2), restored and diffed the same way. 'Nothing else runs' could not be achieved: the card is 48-52 % busy with the owner's desktop programs (WoW, launchers, Discord, browsers) even when idle, other agents' node checks (audition-check.mjs) held the same lock for up to 10 minutes, and CPU was 77-88 % busy during some CPU runs.
checks.disk_and_cache: df after all work: 231 G free of 1.9 T. Cache holds nothing forbidden: no gated or non-commercial sibling (no phonon-40m, no CustomVoice, no kitten 1.7B), no conds.pt, no catalogue embeddings (phonon-voices has 12 character files plus voices.jsonl). Older entries (ACE-Step, Qwen2-Audio, Qwen3-4B, CLAP, Whisper small, Parler mini multilingual, stable-audio-open stub) were there before this task and belong to the sound library.
checks.scoring_recount: Six lines recounted by hand from Whisper's text: phonon-q8 computer_cargo_raw 7 errors of 18 (script: 7); phonon computer_cargo_raw 5 of 18 (script: 5); chatterbox-nano computer_cargo_raw 3 of 18 (script: 3); kokoro cuda computer_cargo_raw 0 of 18 (script: 0); kitten radio_pirate 2 of 18 (script: 2); qwen3 cuda procedural_convoy script 3 of 14 but hand count 2 of 14 (drift swallowed into xanthodrift, escorts to escort; the script's tie rule aligns 'and' with 'genya' and counts it). So 5 of 6 are right; one overcounts by one error (0.214 against 0.143), which is the 'worst WER' that RESULTS.md prints for qwen3 cuda. Medians are unaffected. phonon radio_mayday counts the third 'mayday' as an ordinary error because Whisper wrote 'rave error' for 'Mayday Wayfarer'; arguable.
checks.documents: RESULTS.md matches scores.json and identity.json in every figure I compared (names, WER median and worst, same voice, voices apart, to-clip 0.898 and 0.944). Statements not supported: 'Timings: other agents used the CPU' omits the shared graphics card; 8-thread 'no speedup'; the Kokoro and Qwen3 CUDA RTFs as single figures. CANDIDATES.md matches the dossier and reports (revisions, licences, sizes); one soft spot: the Mimi codec's CC-BY-4.0 comes from the kyutai/mimi card, not from a statement about the Mimi weights inside the Phonon repository (the Phonon report lists that as not verified). The identity figures use the Chatterbox voice encoder, which also conditions Chatterbox, so the 0.898 to-clip figure favours it (RESULTS.md warns in general terms).
